setup_summary.text: HD reports fiscal Q3 on Tuesday Nov 17, expected before the open (Finnhub gives no hour). The calendar labels it 'fiscal Q3 2027', but the company's fiscal 2026 ends Jan 31, 2027. Consensus is EPS $3.95 and revenue $44.04B.

Consensus implies revenue +6.5% and diluted EPS +9.2% against year-ago $41.35B and $3.62 (GAAP). Q2 grew revenue +5.7% and EPS +4.6%, so the bar is higher than on the last print even though the GMS acquisition contribution fades.
Q2 (ended Aug 2, 2026) reported revenue of $47.86B (+5.7%), operating income of $6.84B (+4.3%) and diluted EPS of $4.79 (+4.6%). Operating margin slipped to 14.3% from 14.5%.

Q2 cost of goods sold benefited from about $685M of IEEPA tariff refunds, roughly 1.4% of sales. Management says the refund benefit was 'largely offset' by fuel, energy and other input costs and by GMS mix. Approximately $730M had been received by Aug 2, 'the vast majority' of expected refunds.

My arithmetic: removing the $685M refund from Q2 leaves operating income of about $6.15B (about 12.9% margin, roughly -6% YoY). Q2 EPS would be about $4.25-4.30 (after tax at 24.5% on ~996M shares) against $4.58. The reported EPS growth therefore leans on a likely non-recurring item. Caveat: the refunds offset tariff costs incurred earlier, so this is not a clean like-for-like.

Q2 comparable sales rose +1.7% (vs +1.0% a year ago). Comparable average ticket was +2.8% and comparable transactions -1.0%; FX added about 25bp. The first-half comp was +1.2%, and online sales grew 11.0%.

SG&A grew 8.5% to 17.6% of sales (vs 17.1%), which management attributes to higher operating costs relative to comparable sales performance. First-half operating income grew only +1.1% even with the refund benefit.

The 'Other' segment (SRS including GMS and, since May 11, Mingledorff's HVAC) had Q2 sales of $5.06B vs $3.12B and operating income of $247M vs $201M. Its operating margin was about 4.9% vs 6.4%. Roofing fell to ~39% of Other sales from ~62%.

First-half operating cash flow was $11.42B (+27.4%) and free cash flow was $9.70B (vs $7.25B), helped by working-capital timing. Long-term debt including current installments fell to about $48.6B from $51.3B at Feb 1 after $3.0B of repayments. Buybacks remain paused, with no plan to resume in fiscal 2026.

The Q2 10-Q is signed by CFO Richard McPhail as 'Interim Principal Executive Officer'. The March 10-K was signed by Edward Decker as Chair, President and CEO. The 10-Q forward-looking list newly cites 'organizational changes, including within the Company's senior leadership team'.
Positioning: the stock closed at $329.20 on Oct 30, about 20.7x forward P/E. Options imply a ±7.2% move for the print against a ±2.1% average closing move over the last 8 reports.

last_reported.text: Q2 net sales were $47.86B, +5.7% YoY, of which GMS contributed about $1.4B of incremental sales. Year-ago Q3 was $41.35B.

consensus.text: Consensus is $44.04B, implying +6.5% YoY. Q2 consensus was $47.24B against $47.86B actual.

view.text: GMS closed Sept 4, 2025, so only about one month of its sales is incremental in Q3, versus a full $1.4B in Q2 (my estimate: ~$0.5B). A rough bridge uses Primary growth near Q2's +1.5%, Other ex-GMS growth holding at Q2's roughly +$0.5B, plus FX and Mingledorff's. It lands near $43.0-43.5B, below consensus. Revenue looks like the line where risk to expectations is largest unless comps accelerate. Verify the bridge, since I cannot see the consensus build.

last_reported.text: Q2 diluted EPS was $4.79 vs $4.58 (+4.6%). Year-ago Q3 was $3.62.

consensus.text: Consensus is $3.95, implying +9.2% against the $3.62 GAAP base. The basis (GAAP or adjusted) is not disclosed.

view.text: Q2 EPS included roughly $0.52 of after-tax refund benefit (my arithmetic), and underlying EPS was down about 6-7% YoY. Consensus asks for underlying growth of ~9% in Q3 with little refund help (only ~$45M of the $730M went to inventory cost and flows through COGS as inventory sells). MarketBeat quotes Q2 'EPS' of $4.92 vs the 10-Q's GAAP $4.79, so the consensus basis may differ from GAAP. Confirm the basis before judging a beat or miss.

last_reported.text: Q2 comps were +1.7% (transactions -1.0%, ticket +2.8%, FX ~+25bp). The first-half comp was +1.2%, which implies roughly +0.5-0.7% in Q1.

view.text: Comps are ticket-led, with transactions down for a second straight period (-1.2% in H1). Model +1-2% with negative transactions and a shrinking FX help. The year-ago Q3 comp base is not in the sources. Management attributes demand to smaller repair and maintenance projects amid housing affordability pressure.

last_reported.text: Q2 gross margin was 33.7% vs 33.4%, including the refund benefit. H1 gross margin was 33.4% vs 33.6%.

view.text: Excluding the ~143bp refund effect (my arithmetic), Q2 gross margin was about 32.3%, roughly 110bp below last year on fuel, energy, input costs and GMS mix. With little refund in Q3, the YoY margin comparison should turn negative unless costs ease. The year-ago Q3 gross margin is not in the sources.

last_reported.text: Q2 SG&A was $8.42B (+8.5%) at 17.6% of sales vs 17.1%. Primary-segment SG&A grew ~5.3% ($7.77B vs $7.38B) against a +1.7% comp. Operating margin was 14.3%.

view.text: SG&A deleverage is the second leg of the underlying margin squeeze. Primary SG&A growth is running well above comps, and amortization in Other rose to $125M from $87M. Watch whether SG&A growth stays above sales growth.

metrics_to_model.metric: Other segment (SRS/GMS/HVAC) sales and operating income

last_reported.text: Q2 Other sales were $5.055B (vs $3.120B) and operating income was $247M (vs $201M). Q2 Other D&A was $236M.

view.text: Growth should decelerate sharply from +62% as GMS enters the base (about two months of Q3 were already included last year). Mingledorff's (HVAC, ~$1.1B purchase) adds a full quarter, though management called its Q2 contribution immaterial. Margin was ~4.9% in Q2 vs 6.4%, and the roofing mix shifted to 39% of Other sales. Expect continued dilution unless roofing recovers.

last_reported.text: Q2 interest expense was $583M, and interest and other, net was $524M vs $550M, helped by interest received on IEEPA refunds. The effective tax rate was 24.5% (H1 24.7%).

view.text: The refund-interest tailwind should fade. $1.75B of senior notes mature in September 2026 (2.125% $1.0B and 4.95% $0.75B), alongside $4.2B of commercial paper at 3.8% and no buybacks, so debt paydown is the stated priority. Model a tax rate of about 24.5-24.7%.

last_reported.text: H1 operating cash flow was $11.42B and capex $1.72B (flat). Payables rose $2.5B (accounts payable and accrued expenses change). Inventory was $26.85B vs $25.82B at Feb 1, and turns were 4.5x vs 4.6x.

view.text: Full-year capex of ~$4B implies about $2.3B in H2, back-half weighted. H1 operating cash flow was flattered by vendor-payment timing and by tax-payment timing (the Q4 FY24 deferral hit Q1 FY25). Expect some working-capital normalization, so do not extrapolate the +27% growth.

key_debates.question: Is Q2's EPS growth real earnings power or a one-off tariff refund?

bull.text: Reported Q2 EPS rose 4.6% and revenue beat the $47.24B consensus by about $0.6B. Comps accelerated to +1.7% from +1.0% a year ago, with ticket +2.8% and online +11%.

bear.text: Excluding the $685M refund, my arithmetic puts Q2 operating income down ~6% and EPS down ~7%. SG&A grew 8.5% vs sales +5.7%, and H1 operating income was only +1.1% even with the refund.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 gross margin and SG&A rate with no meaningful refund, EPS vs $3.95, and management quantifying any remaining refund benefit and where it sits in the P&L.

key_debates.question: Can consensus revenue growth of +6.5% be met as the GMS acquisition laps?

bull.text: Q2 revenue beat consensus. Mingledorff's (closed May 11) contributes a full quarter, Other ex-GMS sales grew about $0.5B in Q2, and comps are improving.

bear.text: GMS (closed Sept 4, 2025) was $1.4B of incremental Q2 sales but only roughly $0.5B incremental in Q3 (my estimate). A rough bridge gives ~$43.0-43.5B vs $44.04B consensus unless comps run well above 2%.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 net sales vs $44.04B, Other segment sales, and whether the comp is above ~2% with positive transactions.

key_debates.question: Is the strong cash flow sustainable?

bull.text: H1 free cash flow was $9.70B vs $7.25B, funding $4.6B of dividends, $3.0B of long-term debt repayment and $1.3B of acquisitions. Total debt is falling and capex is flat.

bear.text: The H1 operating cash flow gain came from payables and tax timing. Inventory is up ~4% with turns at 4.5x vs 4.6x. Customer receivables are $3.56B vs $2.59B at Feb 1, and supplier-finance obligations are $542M vs $414M. ROIC fell to 24.8% from 27.2%.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 operating cash flow, payables and inventory trends, and whether debt reduction continues so buybacks can be discussed for FY2027.

key_debates.question: Do SRS/GMS add growth or dilute returns?

bull.text: Other sales rose 62% and operating income rose 23% to $247M. The new HVAC vertical broadens the platform and acquired intangibles amortize over long lives.

bear.text: Other operating margin fell to ~4.9% from 6.4% and roofing dropped to 39% of sales from 62%. Other goodwill is $14.3B, and Other intangible amortization rose to $125M from $87M.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 Other segment operating margin, disclosure of organic growth ex-acquisitions, and roofing demand commentary.

claim.text: Earnings quality: Q2 results include about $685M of non-recurring IEEPA refunds, with the vast majority of refunds already received. Q3 lacks that help while consensus EPS requires +9.2% growth.
Leadership transition: the CFO is signing as Interim Principal Executive Officer and the 10-Q now flags organizational changes in senior leadership. Strategic and guidance continuity is uncertain.
Cost pressures: management cites incremental fuel, energy and other product input costs that offset much of the refund benefit in gross margin.

Demand: customers favor smaller repair and maintenance projects, with larger discretionary projects pressured by interest rates and housing affordability. Comparable transactions are declining (-1.0% in Q2).
Tariff and trade policy uncertainty remains after the Supreme Court IEEPA decision, including additional tariffs under other authority. Management says it cannot predict the ultimate impact.

Working-capital reversal and credit exposure: H1 cash flow benefited from payables timing, while customer receivables rose to $3.56B (from $2.59B at Feb 1) and supplier-finance obligations to $542M. Pro and trade-credit customers carry default risk.

Integration and control risk: SRS, GMS and Mingledorff's drive dilutive margins, rising intangible amortization and large goodwill. GMS was excluded from the 10-K ICFR assessment, and finance-system migration is ongoing.
Expectation risk: the options-implied move of ±7.2% is far above the ±2.1% historical average, so a miss on quality (not just headline) could produce an outsized reaction.

questions_for_management.question: How much of the $730M of IEEPA refunds and related interest hit each quarter and line item, how much remains, and what is Q3 gross margin and EPS excluding them?

why.text: Q2 COGS benefited by about $685M, which flatters margin and EPS, and consensus Q3 EPS of $3.95 needs a clean read of the underlying trend.

questions_for_management.question: What are quarter-to-date comps and the transaction versus ticket trend, and what would turn transactions positive?

why.text: Transactions have been negative for several periods (-1.0% in Q2, -1.2% in H1) and growth is ticket-led.

questions_for_management.question: Why is SG&A growing faster than sales (Primary SG&A +5.3% vs comp +1.7%) and what is the plan for leverage?

why.text: SG&A deleverage drove the operating margin decline in Q2.

questions_for_management.question: What is the CEO succession status and timeline, and does it change strategy, capital allocation or guidance?

why.text: The CFO is Interim Principal Executive Officer and the 10-Q newly references senior-leadership organizational changes.

questions_for_management.question: What is organic growth and margin in SRS, GMS and the HVAC vertical, and when does the roofing mix recover?

why.text: Other margin fell to ~4.9% from 6.4% and roofing dropped to 39% of Other sales from 62%.

questions_for_management.question: How much of the H1 cash flow benefit was timing in payables and taxes, and what should we expect for H2 operating cash flow and inventory?

why.text: Operating cash flow grew 27% on working-capital timing while inventory is up and turns slipped to 4.5x.

questions_for_management.question: What leverage level is needed to resume buybacks, and how should we think about FY2027 capital allocation given ROIC of 24.8% and equity build?

why.text: Repurchases are paused through fiscal 2026 to reduce debt, and ROIC fell on higher average equity.

questions_for_management.question: How are you handling cost inflation in fuel, energy and inputs and any new tariffs, and what pricing is assumed in H2?

why.text: Cost pressures offset much of the refund benefit, and tariff policy remains in flux after the Supreme Court ruling.

The quarterly GMS contribution already in the year-ago Q3 base is not disclosed, so the ~$0.5B incremental estimate and the revenue bridge are my approximations.
The basis of consensus EPS (GAAP vs adjusted) is unknown. MarketBeat's $4.92 Q2 'EPS' cannot be reconciled to the 10-Q's GAAP $4.79, and its definition is not available.
The exact timing and line-item split of IEEPA refunds and refund interest is not disclosed, and nor is the amount of remaining refunds beyond 'the vast majority' received.
Beat/miss record, analyst actions and price-target history are unavailable (FMP refused the request). Only a TradingKey average target is available, and there is no whisper EPS.

The fiscal-period label differs by source: Finnhub says 'fiscal Q3 2027' while the company's fiscal 2026 ends Jan 31, 2027.
The XBRL long-term debt fact for Aug 2, 2026 is missing (F.22). Debt of about $48.6B is computed from the balance sheet (current installments plus long-term).
The NAW article (dated 2026-10-18) describes a quarter ended May 4 with comps of -0.3%. That matches last year's Q1, not the current fiscal year, so it was excluded as stale and mismatched.
No new company filings, 8-Ks or guidance changes since the Aug 25 10-Q are in the sources.
